scenario: 面试官让你设计一个全球文件分享服务，用户会上传、下载、同步文件；题目还没给规模、延迟和一致性要求。
scenario_en: You are asked to design a global file-sharing service for upload, download, and sync, but scale, latency, and consistency are still unstated.
q: 第一步该把什么问清楚？
q_en: What should you clarify first?
options: 先选对象存储、数据库和 CDN
先问功能需求、规模、延迟、一致性和故障容忍
先画微服务拆分图
先估算每台服务器的 CPU 型号
options_en: Pick object storage, databases, and a CDN first.
Clarify functional needs, scale, latency, consistency, and failure tolerance first.
Draw the microservice decomposition first.
Estimate the CPU model for each server first.
why: 我会先把约束问清楚，因为这些约束会决定存储、缓存、复制和同步协议。直接选组件容易把题目做成背模板。
why_en: Clarify the constraints first because they determine storage, caching, replication, and sync choices.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目已经给出完整约束，才进入组件选择和容量估算。
tradeoff: 需求澄清 vs 过早定架构
optionMeanings: 把答案从组件名开始。
先定义系统必须满足的约束。
先决定服务边界。
先进入硬件容量细节。
optionDirectness: 适合约束已经固定后的方案细化。
适合开放题开局，避免选错主路径。
适合业务域已稳定、团队要拆工时。
适合容量模型已明确后的采购估算。
optionScenarioImpacts: 可能选出与一致性或延迟不匹配的组件。
能把后续取舍绑到具体目标上。
服务图看起来完整，但关键约束仍然缺失。
会跳过影响架构的一阶问题。
optionMeanings_en: Define the constraints the system must meet.
optionDirectness_en: Useful after the constraints are fixed.
Best for an open-ended design prompt.
Useful when domain boundaries are already known.
Useful after the capacity model is clear.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You may pick components that miss consistency or latency needs.
It ties later trade-offs to concrete goals.
The diagram may look complete while constraints stay missing.
It skips the first-order architecture questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态或可缓存内容放到离用户更近的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content at edge locations closer to users.

scenario: 你在白板上解释一个电商系统，已经有成熟的负载均衡器、缓存、队列和对象存储可选；时间只有 40 分钟。
scenario_en: You are explaining an e-commerce system on a whiteboard with mature load balancers, caches, queues, and object stores available, and only 40 minutes.
q: 为什么用 building blocks 组织设计？
q_en: Why organize the design around building blocks?
options: 能把每个成熟组件当作有接口和代价的模块讨论
能保证所有组件都不用再解释故障模式
能让系统自动满足所有非功能需求
能避免做任何容量估算
options_en: They let you discuss each mature component as a module with interfaces and costs.
They guarantee every component's failure mode no longer needs explanation.
They make the system automatically satisfy every non-functional requirement.
They remove the need for capacity estimation.
why: building block 的价值是复用稳定抽象，同时仍然说明接口、压力点和代价。它不是魔法盒，缓存、队列、数据库在高压和故障下都要讲行为。
why_en: Building blocks save time by reusing known modules, but you still need to explain their interfaces, pressure points, and trade-offs.
whenOtherWins: 如果组件行为本身就是题目重点，例如设计队列或缓存，就要展开内部机制。
tradeoff: 复用抽象 vs 展开机制
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> LB["Load balancer"]
    LB --> App["App servers"]
    App --> Cache["Cache"]
    App --> Queue["Queue"]
    App --> Store["Object store"]
optionMeanings: 按职责拼装 DNS/LB/存储等成熟能力。
假设名字出现就等于风险消失。
把可用性、延迟、安全当成默认结果。
把吞吐和存储规模留到事后猜。
optionDirectness: 适合主线题先搭骨架，再逐块钻深。
只适合极粗略草图，不能进面试答案。
没有明确 SLO 时，这个说法最容易误导。
只有玩具流量演示才可能暂时不算容量。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官能顺着每块追问极限和替代方案。
一追问异常流量就会答不下去。
会漏掉为什么要多副本或限流。
无法判断机器数、分区和预算。

q: 为什么初版架构后还要留时间迭代？
q_en: Why should you leave time to iterate after the first architecture?
text: 系统设计里，初版方案先覆盖主路径；测出瓶颈后再迭代，因为真实压力常暴露 {{热点}}, {{容量上限}}, 或 {{故障模式}}。
text_en: In system design, the first version covers the main path; iteration follows measurement because real load exposes {{hotspots}}, {{capacity limits}}, or {{failure modes}}.
why: 我会把初版当假设而不是终点。测量后再优化，才能知道该扩容、加缓存、分片还是改协议。
why_en: Treat the first design as a hypothesis, then measure before deciding whether to scale, cache, shard, or change protocols.

scenario: 你要为消息服务选择存储和处理路径，功能已经确定，但数据特征还没问清楚。
scenario_en: You need to choose storage and processing paths for a messaging service; features are clear, but data characteristics are not.
q: 哪些问题会直接影响组件选择？
q_en: Which questions directly affect component choices?
options: 数据是读多还是写多
是否必须读到最新写入
数据保存多久、能丢多少
团队最喜欢哪种架构图配色
options_en: Whether the workload is read-heavy or write-heavy.
Whether reads must see the latest write.
How long data is retained and how much loss is acceptable.
Which architecture-diagram color palette the team likes.
why: 读写比例决定缓存、索引和分片压力；一致性和耐久性决定复制、事务和确认路径。配色不改变系统行为。
why_en: Read/write mix, consistency, and durability shape storage and replication choices; diagram colors do not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据被确认后，在故障后仍能保留下来的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means acknowledged data survives failures.

scenario: 题目是“设计 WhatsApp”，但只有 40 分钟；产品有聊天、群聊、状态、支付、备份、搜索等很多功能。
scenario_en: The prompt is "Design WhatsApp," but you only have 40 minutes; the product includes chat, groups, status, payments, backups, search, and more.
q: 怎样控制设计范围最合理？
q_en: How should you control the design scope?
options: 声明只覆盖核心消息收发和在线状态，并确认哪些功能不做
尝试把所有真实产品功能都画进图里
跳过需求，直接设计 Kafka 集群
只讲 UI 页面，不讲后端路径
options_en: State that you will cover core messaging and presence, and confirm what is out of scope.
Try to include every real product feature in the diagram.
Skip requirements and design a Kafka cluster immediately.
Discuss only UI screens and skip backend paths.
why: 我会先保住核心不变量：消息能送达、顺序可解释、失败可恢复。范围收窄后，架构深度才够。
why_en: Narrow the scope to the core invariants so you can reason deeply about delivery, ordering, and recovery.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求搜索或备份，再把该功能加入主路径或扩展路径。
tradeoff: 核心路径深度 vs 全产品覆盖
optionMeanings: 把题目收敛到核心实时通信路径。
把真实产品的所有边缘功能都纳入本轮。
直接跳到一个消息系统组件。
只讨论客户端界面。
optionDirectness: 适合开放产品题的 40 分钟面试。
适合长期产品规划，不适合单轮系统设计。
只有需求已确认且 Kafka 是瓶颈时才展开。
适合产品评审，不足以回答系统设计。
optionScenarioImpacts: 能深入消息投递、在线状态和故障恢复。
会牺牲主路径深度。
会漏掉消息顺序、存储和离线投递约束。
后端容量和一致性问题仍未回答。

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 是分布式事件流平台，常用于日志、消息和异步数据管道。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform used for logs, messaging, and async data pipelines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面，指用户直接交互的页面和控件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User Interface means the screens and controls that users interact with.

scenario: 一个服务启动后流量突然翻倍，你说“加更多服务器”但没有定位瓶颈；当前 DB CPU 很低，应用 CPU 已接近 90%。
scenario_en: Traffic doubles after launch; you say "add more servers" without locating the bottleneck; DB CPU is low, while app CPU is near 90%.
q: 这个跟进问题暴露了什么风险？
q_en: What risk does this follow-up expose?
options: 应该先分库分表，因为所有扩容都从 DB 开始
需要先诊断瓶颈；这次更像应用计算层扩容
应该把所有请求都改成强一致事务
应该删掉监控，避免被数字干扰
options_en: Shard the database first because all scaling starts at the DB.
Diagnose the bottleneck first; this case looks like app-compute scaling.
Turn every request into a strongly consistent transaction.
Remove monitoring so the numbers do not distract you.
why: 扩容动作要对准瓶颈；DB 没忙时先分片只会增加复杂度。这里应用 CPU 接近饱和，先横向扩应用或优化计算路径更合理。
why_en: Scaling should target the bottleneck; with app CPU saturated and DB idle, app-tier scaling is the first move.
whenOtherWins: 如果监控显示 DB 写入、锁等待或存储 I/O 才是瓶颈，数据库分片或索引优化会反超。
tradeoff: 诊断式扩容 vs 组件名扩容

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器；CPU 饱和常意味着计算路径排队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU executes instructions, and saturation often means compute requests are queuing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统读写磁盘、网络或外设的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O is work spent reading or writing disks, networks, or devices.

scenario: 支付服务依赖风控接口；风控接口开始 2 秒超时，调用方把失败请求无限重试，整体延迟和错误率继续上升。
scenario_en: A payment service depends on a risk-check API; that API starts timing out after 2 seconds, and callers retry failed requests indefinitely.
q: 最该先加哪类保护？
q_en: What protection should you add first?
options: 无限增加重试次数
断路器、超时上限和降级路径
把数据库改成最终一致
关闭所有告警
options_en: Increase retries without a limit.
Use circuit breakers, timeout budgets, and a degraded path.
Make the database eventually consistent.
Turn off all alerts.
why: 依赖已经慢了，更多重试会放大排队和下游压力。我会设置超时和断路器，必要时走缓存结果、人工审核或拒绝高风险请求。
why_en: When a dependency is already slow, bounded timeouts and circuit breakers prevent retries from amplifying the outage.
whenOtherWins: 如果失败是瞬时丢包且下游容量充足，少量带退避的重试才有价值。
tradeoff: 可用性保护 vs 完整实时校验

termDefinitions.meaning: 断路器在依赖连续失败时短期开路，避免调用方继续压垮下游。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker temporarily stops calls to a failing dependency to prevent overload.

q: 为什么“NoSQL box”不是一个完整设计？
q_en: Why is a "NoSQL box" not a complete design?
text: 存储设计要说明 {{访问模式}}, {{主键/排序键}}, {{分页}}, {{版本或幂等键}}；只写一个数据库名字无法判断读写路径。
text_en: A storage design should state {{access patterns}}, {{primary/sort keys}}, {{pagination}}, and {{versioning or idempotency keys}}; a database name alone does not define the read/write path.
why: 数据库类型只是起点，真正决定可扩展性的是查询怎么进来、数据怎么分布、重复请求怎么处理。
why_en: The database category is only a starting point; scalability depends on access patterns, keys, and duplicate-handling semantics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等键用于识别重复请求，让重试不会重复创建订单或扣款。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key identifies duplicate requests so retries do not create duplicate side effects.

scenario: 订单服务需要同时扣库存和创建订单；并发请求可能同时抢最后一件商品。
scenario_en: An order service must decrement inventory and create an order; concurrent requests may race for the last item.
q: 数据库事务这个抽象帮你隐藏什么？
q_en: What does the database transaction abstraction hide for you?
options: 提交/回滚接口背后的并发控制和一致状态切换
所有跨机网络分区问题
所有业务幂等逻辑
所有读缓存失效策略
options_en: The concurrency control and consistent-state transition behind commit or rollback.
Every cross-machine network partition problem.
All business idempotency logic.
All read-cache invalidation policies.
why: 事务让业务代码用 commit/abort 表达原子变化，数据库负责隔离并发和保持约束。但它不自动解决跨服务网络失败或缓存一致性。
why_en: A transaction lets business code express an atomic commit or abort while the database handles concurrency and constraints.
whenOtherWins: 跨多个服务的长流程更适合 saga、消息或补偿动作，而不是把所有步骤塞进单库事务。
tradeoff: 本地一致状态 vs 跨服务可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务把一组数据库操作包装成要么全部提交、要么全部回滚的单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction groups database operations so they either all commit or all roll back.

scenario: 两个后端服务要频繁互调，团队希望接口像本地函数一样强类型、低开销，并自动处理序列化。
scenario_en: Two backend services call each other frequently; the team wants low-overhead, strongly typed APIs that feel like local functions and handle serialization.
q: 哪种通信抽象最贴合？
q_en: Which communication abstraction fits best?
options: RPC/gRPC
手写原始 TCP 字节流
浏览器 localStorage
只靠离线批处理文件
options_en: RPC or gRPC.
Hand-written raw TCP byte streams.
Browser localStorage.
Offline batch files only.
why: RPC 把远程调用包装成函数接口，stub/runtime 处理序列化、传输和响应。代价是调用看起来像本地，但仍会遇到超时、重试和部分失败。
why_en: RPC fits frequent backend calls because it gives a typed function-like interface while still requiring timeout and retry design.
whenOtherWins: 如果调用是公开 Web API 或需要浏览器直接消费，REST/HTTP 可能更合适；如果是流式事件，消息队列或 pub-sub 更自然。
tradeoff: 函数式接口便利 vs 分布式失败显式处理
optionMeanings: 用接口定义生成远程函数调用代码。
直接读写传输层字节。
浏览器本地的键值存储。
把交互改成离线文件交换。
optionDirectness: 适合内部服务频繁互调和强类型接口。
适合极端定制协议，但开发和排错成本高。
适合客户端少量本地状态，不适合后端互调。
适合离线报表，不适合低延迟请求。
optionScenarioImpacts: 减少手写序列化和 socket 管理。
团队要自己处理协议兼容和重试。
无法连接两个后端服务。
请求响应会变成批处理延迟。

termDefinitions.meaning: 远程过程调用，让程序像调用本地函数一样调用另一台机器上的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Remote Procedure Call lets a program invoke a procedure on another machine like a local function.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见高性能 RPC 框架，通常用接口定义生成客户端和服务端代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework that generates client and server code from interface definitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输控制协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transmission Control Protocol provides reliable, ordered byte-stream transport.

q: 同步 RPC 的调用链正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of a synchronous RPC call?
steps: 服务端 stub 解包参数并调用目标函数
客户端 stub 把参数序列化成网络消息
客户端 runtime 把消息发到服务端并等待响应
服务端函数执行后把结果交回服务端 stub
客户端 stub 解包响应，调用线程继续执行
why: RPC 的关键链条是 stub 做打包/解包，runtime 做传输，服务端执行真实函数。同步调用期间客户端线程会阻塞到响应或超时。
why_en: In synchronous RPC, stubs marshal and unmarshal data while runtimes transmit messages, and the caller blocks until a response or timeout.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant CS as Client stub
    participant R as RPC runtime
    participant SS as Server stub
    participant S as Server
    C->>CS: call method(args)
    CS->>R: marshal request
    R->>SS: transmit message
    SS->>S: invoke function
    S-->>SS: result
    SS-->>R: marshal response
    R-->>CS: response
    CS-->>C: return value

termDefinitions.meaning: stub 是本地代理代码，负责把函数参数和返回值转换成可传输消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stub is local proxy code that turns function arguments and return values into transportable messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: marshaling 是把内存中的参数编码成标准消息格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Marshaling encodes in-memory arguments into a standard message format.

scenario: 订单服务通过 RPC 调支付服务；客户端超时了，但网络中断前支付服务可能已经扣款。
scenario_en: An order service calls a payment service over RPC; the client times out, but the payment service may already have charged the card before the network failed.
q: 为什么超时不能被 RPC 完全隐藏？
q_en: Why can't RPC fully hide timeouts?
options: 因为调用方无法仅凭超时判断远端是否执行成功
因为 RPC 一定不会序列化参数
因为所有远程调用都必须改成 UDP
因为本地函数也会产生网络分区
options_en: Because the caller cannot know from a timeout alone whether the remote side completed.
Because RPC never serializes arguments.
Because every remote call must use UDP.
Because local functions also create network partitions.
why: 超时只说明调用方没及时拿到响应，不说明远端没做副作用。我会加幂等键、查询状态或补偿流程，避免重试造成重复扣款。
why_en: A timeout only means the caller lacks a response, so idempotency keys or status checks are needed before retrying side effects.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作是纯读且无副作用，简单重试的风险低很多。
tradeoff: 调用抽象简洁 vs 副作用可判定性
optionMeanings: 把超时视为未知结果。
否认 RPC 的参数编码步骤。
把问题误归因到传输协议选择。
把远程失败套到本地函数上。
optionDirectness: 适合有副作用的远程写调用。
只在讨论实现 bug 时相关。
适合比较 TCP/UDP 传输语义时。
只适合本地进程内调用。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会补幂等键或状态查询。
会错过真正的重复扣款风险。
换 UDP 还会丢掉可靠传输语义。
会低估网络分区和部分失败。

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等键把多次相同请求识别成一次业务动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key lets repeated requests map to one business action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户数据报协议，提供无连接、不保证送达或顺序的数据报传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User Datagram Protocol sends connectionless datagrams without delivery or ordering guarantees.

scenario: 你要设计 DNS 记录传播；更新后短时间内有些地区读到旧值可以接受，但最终所有缓存要收敛。
scenario_en: You are designing DNS record propagation; some regions may temporarily read old values after an update, but all caches must eventually converge.
q: 应选择哪种一致性模型？
q_en: Which consistency model should you choose?
options: 线性一致性
顺序一致性
因果一致性
最终一致性
options_en: Linearizability.
Sequential consistency.
Causal consistency.
Eventual consistency.
why: DNS 更看重高可用和全球传播，短暂旧值通常可接受。最终一致性承诺停止写入后副本收敛，代价是读到旧记录。
why_en: DNS fits eventual consistency because temporary stale reads are acceptable as long as replicas converge after updates stop.
whenOtherWins: 如果是改密码或撤销权限，确认后所有读都必须看到新值，线性一致性更合适。
tradeoff: 高可用低协调 vs 读最新写

termDefinitions.meaning: 域名系统，把域名解析成可连接的网络地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Domain Name System maps domain names to network addresses.

scenario: 评论系统允许用户回复评论；读者可以稍晚看到新评论，但回复不能出现在被回复的原评论之前。
scenario_en: A comment system supports replies; readers may see new comments slightly late, but a reply must not appear before its parent comment.
q: 哪种一致性约束最贴合？
q_en: Which consistency guarantee fits best?
options: 完全不保证顺序的最终一致性
因果一致性
所有操作都线性一致
只保证磁盘耐久性
options_en: Eventual consistency with no ordering guarantee.
Causal consistency.
Linearize every operation.
Only guarantee disk durability.
why: 回复依赖原评论，所以依赖关系必须保序；不同独立评论可以晚点或换序显示。因果一致性比最终一致性多保这条关系，又比全局线性一致便宜。
why_en: Causal consistency preserves reply-after-parent ordering without forcing every independent comment into one global real-time order.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求所有用户看到完全相同的实时评论顺序，才需要更强的一致性或中心化排序。
tradeoff: 依赖关系正确 vs 全局实时排序成本

scenario: 用户刚修改密码并收到成功响应；安全要求是旧密码立即失效，之后任何登录读都不能再接受旧密码。
scenario_en: A user has just changed their password and received success; the old password must become invalid immediately for all later login reads.
q: 这个字段需要什么一致性？
q_en: What consistency does this field need?
options: 最终一致性即可
只要本地缓存命中即可
线性一致性/强一致读写
只要异步日志最终写入即可
options_en: Eventual consistency is enough.
A local cache hit is enough.
Linearizable or strongly consistent reads and writes.
Eventually writing an async log is enough.
why: 密码变更确认后，后续登录必须读到新状态。线性一致性通常要同步复制或共识，代价是延迟和分区时可用性下降。
why_en: Password changes need linearizable behavior because once the write is acknowledged, every later login must see the new state.
whenOtherWins: 如果是点赞数、浏览量或推荐缓存，短暂旧值可接受，最终一致性通常更划算。
tradeoff: 安全正确性 vs 低延迟高可用

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性一致性要求操作看起来按真实时间顺序一个个生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes operations appear to take effect one at a time in real-time order.

scenario: 你在解释“consistency”一词：一个场景是数据库约束不被破坏，另一个场景是副本在分区时是否暴露不同值。
scenario_en: You are explaining the word "consistency": one case is about database invariants, the other about whether replicas expose different values during partitions.
q: ACID consistency 和 CAP consistency 差在哪？
q_en: How do ACID consistency and CAP consistency differ?
options: ACID 管约束状态，CAP 管分布式副本视图
ACID 只用于缓存，CAP 只用于单机数据库
两者都只表示低延迟
两者都表示数据永不丢失
options_en: ACID is about valid database states, while CAP is about replica views in distributed systems.
ACID is only for caches, and CAP is only for single-node databases.
Both only mean low latency.
Both mean data is never lost.
why: ACID 的一致性是事务前后满足约束；CAP 的一致性是分布式读写看到同一个逻辑值。混用这两个词会把数据库约束和副本可见性讲乱。
why_en: ACID consistency protects database invariants, while CAP consistency is about what values distributed replicas expose.
tradeoff: 本地数据约束 vs 分布式副本可见性

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务数据库常见的四类保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the set of transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 描述分布式系统在网络分区下对一致性和可用性的取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the consistency and availability trade-off under network partitions.

scenario: 集群里一个节点不再响应；监控可能明确知道它永久停机，也可能只是看不到心跳。
scenario_en: A node in a cluster stops responding; monitoring may know it halted permanently, or it may only miss heartbeats.
q: fail-stop 和 crash failure 的关键差异是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between fail-stop and crash failure?
options: fail-stop 可可靠检测停止，crash 可能静默停掉
crash 一定是恶意节点篡改消息并继续响应
fail-stop 只表示消息延迟，不涉及节点停止
两者都表示节点返回随机错误值而不是停机
options_en: Fail-stop is reliably detectable, while a crash may be silent.
A crash always means a malicious node keeps changing messages.
Fail-stop only means delayed messages and not a stopped node.
Both mean random wrong values rather than a halted node.
why: 可检测性决定恢复动作：fail-stop 可以更快摘除节点，静默 crash 需要心跳超时、重试和误判处理。两者都不是任意作恶。
why_en: The key difference is detectability, which changes how quickly the system can remove or replace the failed node.
tradeoff: 可靠检测恢复 vs 心跳超时误判

scenario: 竞价系统要求 50 ms 内返回出价；某节点计算结果正确，但 500 ms 后才返回。
scenario_en: An ad-bidding system requires bids within 50 ms; one node computes the correct result but returns after 500 ms.
q: 这更像哪类失败？
q_en: Which failure model does this resemble?
options: temporal failure
fail-stop failure
Byzantine failure
receive omission only
options_en: Temporal failure.
Fail-stop failure.
Byzantine failure.
Receive omission only.
why: 结果正确但超过业务截止时间，对系统来说仍然不可用。不能把它简单当 crash，因为它可能稍后回来并造成重复或乱序副作用。
why_en: A correct answer that arrives after the deadline is a temporal failure, not simply a crash.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点完全停止且可被可靠检测，fail-stop 才更贴切；如果返回任意假结果，才接近 Byzantine。
tradeoff: 正确结果 vs 截止时间可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: 拜占庭失败指节点可能任意、矛盾或恶意地响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Byzantine failure means a node can behave arbitrarily, inconsistently, or maliciously.

scenario: 你在给消息系统做故障注入，需要区分发送端没发、接收端没收、节点任意作恶和响应过晚。
scenario_en: You are injecting failures into a messaging system and need to distinguish send omissions, receive omissions, arbitrary behavior, and late responses.
q: 哪些映射是正确的？
q_en: Which mappings are correct?
options: send omission：节点没有发出应答
receive omission：节点没有收到请求也无法确认
Byzantine：节点可能返回随机或恶意结果
temporal：节点永久停机且可被可靠检测
options_en: Send omission: the node fails to send a response.
Receive omission: the node fails to receive the request and cannot acknowledge it.
Byzantine: the node may return random or malicious results.
Temporal: the node halts permanently and is reliably detected.
why: omission 关注消息收发丢失，Byzantine 关注任意错误行为。temporal 是返回太晚，不是可靠检测的永久停机。
why_en: Omission failures are about missing sends or receives, Byzantine failures are arbitrary behavior, and temporal failures are late responses.

scenario: 一个服务承诺 99.999% 年可用性；一年按 365 天估算，总时间约 525,600 分钟。
scenario_en: A service promises 99.999% annual availability; using 365 days, the year has about 525,600 minutes.
q: five nines 会迫使哪条设计路径？
q_en: What design path does five nines force?
options: 自动故障检测、快速 failover 和谨慎发布
只靠人工值班，事故后再慢慢恢复
把计划维护都放进业务高峰期
不需要监控，因为停机预算足够宽
options_en: Automated detection, fast failover, and careful releases.
Rely only on humans and recover slowly after incidents.
Schedule planned maintenance during peak business hours.
Skip monitoring because the downtime budget is generous.
why: 公式是 downtime = 525,600 分钟 × (1 - 0.99999) ≈ 5.26 分钟。这个数字会约束故障检测、自动 failover、发布和维护窗口。
why_en: Five nines allows about 5.26 minutes of yearly downtime, which forces fast detection, failover, and careful releases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标，定义服务要达到的可用性、延迟或错误率目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is a target for availability, latency, or error rate.

scenario: 供应商声称 99.99% 可用，但合同排除了计划维护、部分区域故障和某些攻击导致的停机。
scenario_en: A provider claims 99.99% availability, but the contract excludes planned maintenance, partial regional outages, and some attack-related downtime.
q: 评估这个 SLA 时最该注意什么？
q_en: What should you watch when evaluating this SLA?
options: 只看 nines 数字即可
确认停机口径、统计起点和排除项
把 SLA 当作性能延迟承诺
默认所有用户受影响才算停机
options_en: Only look at the number of nines.
Check downtime definitions, measurement start, and exclusions.
Treat the SLA as a latency guarantee.
Assume downtime only counts if every user is affected.
why: availability 的分母和停机定义会改变真实风险。部分故障、维护和安全事件若被排除，你自己的冗余和监控仍要覆盖。
why_en: Availability claims are only meaningful after you inspect what downtime counts and what the provider excludes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是内部容量草算，先用 nines 做粗估可以，但合同评审不能停在那里。
tradeoff: 宣传指标 vs 可执行故障预算

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，是供应商和客户之间可执行的服务承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Agreement is an enforceable service commitment between provider and customer.

scenario: 服务一个月只故障一次，但修复花了 12 小时；另一个服务每周都有小故障，但 1 分钟自动恢复。
scenario_en: One service fails only once a month but takes 12 hours to repair; another has weekly small failures but recovers automatically in one minute.
q: 这说明可靠性和可用性怎么区分？
q_en: What does this show about reliability versus availability?
options: 可靠性看故障频率和持续正确运行，可用性还强烈受修复时间影响
可靠性和可用性完全相同，都只看服务名字
只要 MTBF 高，可用性一定高，不受恢复时间影响
MTTR 只影响代码可读性，不影响用户可访问时间
options_en: Reliability is about failure frequency and continued correct operation, while availability is strongly affected by repair time.
Reliability and availability are identical and only depend on the service name.
High MTBF always means high availability, regardless of recovery time.
MTTR affects only code readability, not user-visible access time.
why: 罕见但长时间故障会拖低可用性；频繁但秒级恢复也可能保持较高可用性。设计上要同时提高 MTBF、降低 MTTR。
why_en: Rare long outages can hurt availability more than frequent short ones, so design for both high MTBF and low MTTR.
tradeoff: 少故障 vs 快恢复

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均故障间隔，表示可修复系统两次故障之间的平均运行时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mean Time Between Failures is the average operating time between failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均修复时间，表示从故障到恢复的平均耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mean Time To Repair is the average time needed to restore service after a failure.

q: 可维护性常拆成哪三类能力？
q_en: What three abilities commonly make up maintainability?
text: 可维护性不只是代码好看；它包括 {{operability}}, {{lucidity}}, 和 {{modifiability}}。
text_en: Maintainability is not just pretty code; it includes {{operability}}, {{lucidity}}, and {{modifiability}}.
why: operability 让系统容易运行和恢复，lucidity 让代码容易理解，modifiability 让新需求更容易接入。三者共同降低 MTTR。
why_en: Operability, lucidity, and modifiability all reduce the time needed to operate, understand, and change a system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统容易运行、监控、排障和恢复的程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operability is how easy a system is to run, monitor, debug, and recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统接入变更和新功能的难易程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modifiability is how easily a system accepts changes and new features.

scenario: 内部工具流量稳定，单台数据库 CPU 持续 70%，内存不足；目标是快速缓解压力，不想马上改分片和复制拓扑。
scenario_en: An internal tool has stable traffic; one database sits around 70% CPU and lacks memory, and the goal is quick relief without changing sharding or replication.
q: 优先考虑哪种扩容？
q_en: Which scaling approach should you consider first?
options: 垂直扩容
立刻做全球多活
把所有请求异步化
删除所有索引
options_en: Vertical scaling.
Build global active-active immediately.
Make every request asynchronous.
Delete every index.
why: 稳定负载下，加 CPU/RAM 能快速提高单机上限，接口和数据模型变化小。代价是有硬件天花板，升级也可能需要维护窗口。
why_en: Vertical scaling is a quick fit for stable load because it raises one machine's ceiling with minimal architecture change.
whenOtherWins: 如果流量快速波动或单机已经到物理上限，水平扩容和分片更合适。
tradeoff: 实施简单快速 vs 单机上限

scenario: 短视频服务用户增长很快，流量有明显峰谷；单机升级越来越贵，还需要某台机器挂了其他机器继续服务。
scenario_en: A short-video service is growing quickly with traffic peaks and valleys; bigger single machines are expensive, and other machines must continue if one fails.
q: 哪种扩容更适合作为长期主线？
q_en: Which scaling approach is the better long-term path?
options: 永远只买更大的机器
水平扩容，加机器并配合负载均衡/分片/复制
降低所有用户请求数到零
把所有数据放进浏览器缓存
options_en: Always buy a bigger machine.
Scale horizontally with more machines plus load balancing, sharding, and replication.
Reduce every user's request count to zero.
Put all data in browser cache.
why: 水平扩容能把请求和数据分摊到多台机器，也能让单点故障影响变小。代价是分区、复制、协调和跨节点延迟更复杂。
why_en: Horizontal scaling is the long-term path for rapid growth because it spreads load and reduces single-node failure impact.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统很小、负载可预测、团队运维能力有限，先垂直扩容更省事。
tradeoff: 横向容量与容错 vs 分布式复杂度

scenario: 电商服务白天和大促时流量暴涨，夜间很低；团队希望按 CPU、网络流量或队列长度自动增减实例。
scenario_en: An e-commerce service spikes during the day and promotions but is quiet at night; the team wants instance count to follow CPU, network traffic, or queue length.
q: 应该引入什么能力？
q_en: What capability should you introduce?
options: autoscaling
只做手工扩容
固定最大实例数不变
把监控延迟到事故后再看
options_en: Autoscaling.
Manual scaling only.
Keep the maximum instance count fixed forever.
Look at monitoring only after incidents.
why: autoscaling 按指标加减容量，能在峰值保可用、低谷降成本。代价是需要合适阈值、冷启动预算和防抖，避免来回抖动。
why_en: Autoscaling follows demand, but it needs good metrics, startup budgets, and damping to avoid oscillation.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载长期稳定且变更窗口严格，手工容量规划可能更可控。
tradeoff: 弹性成本效率 vs 自动化复杂度

scenario: 聊天产品要求双方在线时消息低延迟双向传输，服务器也要主动推送新消息。
scenario_en: A chat product needs low-latency bidirectional message transfer while both sides are online, and the server must push new messages.
q: 哪种协议方向更合适？
q_en: Which protocol direction fits better?
options: WebSocket 长连接
每分钟一次 HTTP 轮询
每天离线批处理文件
只靠 CDN 缓存聊天消息
options_en: A WebSocket long-lived connection.
HTTP polling once per minute.
Daily offline batch files.
Only CDN-cache chat messages.
why: 双向实时消息需要服务器主动推送，WebSocket 避免每次都重新建请求。代价是连接数、心跳和断线重连要纳入容量设计。
why_en: WebSocket fits bidirectional low-latency messaging, but connection count, heartbeats, and reconnects become capacity concerns.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是偶尔刷新状态，短轮询或长轮询的运维成本可能更低。
tradeoff: 低延迟双向推送 vs 长连接运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: WebSocket 是在单个长连接上进行双向通信的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for bidirectional communication over one long-lived connection.

scenario: 社交平台里明星发帖会触达上千万粉丝；所有粉丝都在写入时 fan-out 会压垮写路径，但活跃用户打开首页要很快。
scenario_en: On a social platform, a celebrity post may reach tens of millions of followers; fanning out to everyone on write overloads writes, but active users need fast home feeds.
q: 更合理的 feed 策略是什么？
q_en: What feed strategy is more reasonable?
options: 所有粉丝都写入时立刻预计算
活跃 feed cache，非活跃读时生成
所有用户每次都全表扫描关注关系
禁止明星发布内容
options_en: Precompute for every follower immediately on write.
Use feed cache for active users and generate inactive feeds on read.
Full-scan follow relationships for every user on every read.
Ban celebrities from posting.
why: 关键是把高价值的低延迟读和巨大的写放大拆开。活跃用户吃预计算缓存，非活跃用户把成本推迟到读时。
why_en: Splitting active and inactive users reduces write amplification while keeping active-user reads fast.
whenOtherWins: 如果粉丝量小且读远多于写，全量写时 fan-out 会更简单。
tradeoff: 写放大 vs 首页读取延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Post["Celebrity post"] --> Active["Active followers: feed cache"]
    Post --> Inactive["Inactive followers: generate on read"]
    Active --> FastRead["Fast home feed"]
    Inactive --> LazyRead["Deferred cost"]

scenario: 打车系统每 4 秒收到一次司机位置更新；附近司机查询要快，但空间索引更新也会占 CPU 和锁资源。
scenario_en: A ride-hailing system receives driver location updates every 4 seconds; nearby-driver queries must be fast, but spatial-index updates consume CPU and locking resources.
q: 为什么不能只说“用 Quadtree”就结束？
q_en: Why can't you just say "use a Quadtree" and stop?
options: 因为频繁移动会让索引维护成本成为瓶颈
因为 Quadtree 不能表达二维空间
因为附近查询不需要任何索引
因为所有司机位置必须放在 CDN
options_en: Because frequent movement can make index maintenance the bottleneck.
Because a Quadtree cannot represent two-dimensional space.
Because nearby queries never need an index.
Because all driver locations must be stored in a CDN.
why: Quadtree 让附近查询快，但每 4 秒批量更新会产生重平衡、锁和写放大。面试里要说明更新频率、查询频率和可能的混合方案。
why_en: A Quadtree can speed nearby queries, but high-frequency updates may shift the bottleneck to index maintenance.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象移动少、读查询远多于写更新，Quadtree 这类空间索引更直接。
tradeoff: 查询速度 vs 索引更新成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 四叉树把二维空间递归切成四块，用于空间查找和附近查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Quadtree recursively divides two-dimensional space into four regions for spatial lookup.

scenario: 地图服务的道路图太大，单机放不下；用户从不同地区请求路线，目标是降低延迟并避免单点故障。
scenario_en: A map service's road graph is too large for one machine; users from many regions request routes, and the goal is lower latency without a single point of failure.
q: Google Maps 类路线服务该怎么拆？
q_en: How should a Google-Maps-like routing service be split?
options: 道路图分 segment，并复制 segment servers
只保留一个全球主服务器承接所有路线请求
把所有可能路线预先写成静态 HTML 文件
每次请求都下载完整道路图到客户端计算
options_en: Split the road graph into segments and replicate segment servers.
Keep one global primary server for every routing request.
Prewrite every possible route as static HTML files.
Download the full road graph to the client on every request.
why: segment 拆分让数据和计算分摊到多台机器，复制后还能在节点故障时继续服务。代价是跨 segment 路由要协调边界和缓存。
why_en: Segmenting the road graph spreads storage and routing work, while replication avoids one server becoming the failure point.
whenOtherWins: 如果地图很小且只服务一个地区，单机或少量分区可能更简单。
tradeoff: 数据/计算分摊 vs 跨分区路由复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Route request"] --> LB["Load balancer"]
    LB --> S1["Segment server A"]
    LB --> S2["Segment server B"]
    S1 <--> S2
    S1 --> R1["Replica"]
    S2 --> R2["Replica"]

scenario: 你要解释 YouTube 类服务如何同时降低响应时间和提高可靠性。
scenario_en: You need to explain how a YouTube-like service lowers response time while improving reliability.
q: 哪些组件和目标匹配？
q_en: Which components match the goals?
options: CDN/ISP 缓存：把视频和缩略图放近用户，减少回源
blob storage：存放视频这类大对象
heartbeat：发现并移除异常服务器
单机内存数组：长期保存全部原始视频
options_en: CDN or ISP caches: place videos and thumbnails near users and reduce origin traffic.
Blob storage: store large video objects.
Heartbeats: detect and remove unhealthy servers.
One in-memory array: persist all raw videos forever.
why: 媒体服务的主成本是大对象存储、跨地域传输和故障摘除。缓存和 blob store 降低读路径压力，heartbeat 缩短故障影响时间。
why_en: A video service needs edge caching, blob storage, and heartbeats because media cost is dominated by large objects, distance, and failure detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象/Blob 存储用于保存视频、图片、备份等非结构化大对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage stores large unstructured objects such as videos, images, and backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 心跳是服务定期发送的健康信号，用来检测节点是否仍可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic health signal used to detect whether a node is still alive.

scenario: 系统要在部分组件失败时继续输出正确结果；你可以修正错误状态，也可以用冗余把错误挡住。
scenario_en: A system must keep producing correct results when some components fail; you can either correct the bad state or mask the fault with redundancy.
q: fault-removal 和 fault-masking 怎么区分？
q_en: How do fault-removal and fault-masking differ?
options: removal 修错状态，masking 用冗余挡故障
removal 只用于 UI，masking 只用于日志系统
两者都要求关闭备份节点后再恢复服务
两者都表示不处理故障并等待用户重试
options_en: Removal corrects bad state, while masking uses redundancy to hide faults.
Removal is only for UI, and masking is only for logging systems.
Both require turning off backup nodes before restoring service.
Both mean ignoring failures and waiting for user retries.
why: fault-removal 的思路是把系统带回正确状态；fault-masking 的思路是让冗余副本接住输出。前者偏恢复动作，后者偏持续服务。
why_en: Fault-removal corrects state, while fault-masking uses redundant components so users do not see the fault.
tradeoff: 恢复修正 vs 冗余掩盖

scenario: 支付主库故障时，业务希望几乎零停机；预算允许长期运行一套已同步的备用库。
scenario_en: When the primary payment database fails, the business wants near-zero downtime and can afford a continuously running synchronized standby.
q: 哪种 failover 更贴合？
q_en: Which failover style fits better?
options: hot failover
cold failover
手工从备份磁带恢复
等用户重试到成功
options_en: Hot failover.
Cold failover.
Manual restore from backup tape.
Wait for users to retry until it works.
why: hot failover 让备用实例已经运行并接近可接管状态，所以切换延迟最小。代价是资源常驻和同步复杂度更高。
why_en: Hot failover minimizes downtime because the standby is already running, at the cost of extra resources and synchronization.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统不关键、允许分钟级恢复，warm/cold failover 能省成本。
tradeoff: 低停机 vs 常驻冗余成本

scenario: 购物车服务要在多副本间复制写入；产品可以选择写入确认前等所有关键副本，或先确认再异步传播。
scenario_en: A cart service replicates writes across replicas; the product can wait for key replicas before acknowledgment, or acknowledge first and propagate asynchronously.
q: 同步复制和异步复制的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core trade-off between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
options: 同步保新鲜读但慢，异步快但可能读旧
同步复制一定更便宜，也不增加写入等待
异步复制一定不需要冲突处理或回放
两者都不影响读到的数据或分区行为
options_en: Sync keeps reads fresher but slower; async is faster but may read stale data.
Synchronous replication is always cheaper and adds no write wait.
Asynchronous replication never needs conflict handling or replay.
Neither affects what reads observe or how partitions behave.
why: 同步路径把副本确认放进用户延迟和分区风险里；异步路径先保响应，但副本落后时会读到旧状态。选哪种要看业务能否容忍 stale read。
why_en: Synchronous replication buys fresher reads with coordination cost, while asynchronous replication buys availability with possible stale reads.
tradeoff: 强一致/新鲜读 vs 可用性/低延迟

scenario: 三个进程在保存 checkpoint 时仍互发消息；恢复后，进程 i 的快照记录“收到 m1”，但进程 j 的快照没有记录“发送 m1”。
scenario_en: Three processes keep exchanging messages during checkpointing; after recovery, process i's snapshot says it received m1, but process j's snapshot lacks the send of m1.
q: 这个 checkpoint 有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with this checkpoint?
options: 全局状态不一致，恢复后会出现无来源消息
它一定比同步复制更强一致
它说明所有消息都已安全提交
它只是 UI 显示问题
options_en: The global state is inconsistent and can restore a message with no recorded source.
It is always stronger than synchronous replication.
It proves every message has been safely committed.
It is only a UI display problem.
why: 一致 checkpoint 要么同时包含发送和接收，要么都不包含。只记录接收不记录发送，会让恢复后的状态违反消息历史。
why_en: A consistent checkpoint must not contain a received message without the corresponding recorded send.
whenOtherWins: 如果 checkpoint 协议能冻结或记录 in-flight 消息，恢复状态就能保持一致。
tradeoff: 独立快照简单 vs 全局状态一致
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant J as Process j
    participant I as Process i
    J-->>I: m1
    Note over I: checkpoint records receive
    Note over J: checkpoint misses send
    I->>I: restore sees orphan message

scenario: 银行系统支持查余额、转账、缴费和对账单；用户愿意等几百毫秒，但不能接受错账或凭证泄露。
scenario_en: A banking system supports balances, transfers, bill pay, and statements; users can tolerate a few hundred milliseconds, but not incorrect balances or credential leaks.
q: NFR 优先级应该怎么排？
q_en: How should you prioritize the NFRs?
options: 安全和一致性优先，低延迟不能牺牲账务正确性
低延迟永远第一，余额可以稍后修
只优化界面动画
只追求最终一致，不做审计
options_en: Security and consistency first; latency must not sacrifice financial correctness.
Latency is always first, and balances can be fixed later.
Optimize only UI animations.
Use eventual consistency only and skip auditing.
why: 金融场景的核心风险是错账和泄露，所以认证、审计、事务和强一致路径优先。延迟仍重要，但不能换掉账务正确性。
why_en: For banking, security and consistency outrank raw latency because incorrect balances and leaks are product failures.
whenOtherWins: 如果是点赞数或推荐流，低延迟和可用性通常可以压过强一致。
tradeoff: 账务正确性/安全 vs 极低延迟

scenario: 航天器和地面通信中断，同时硬件模块故障；系统必须在人工干预前保持关键控制能力。
scenario_en: A spacecraft loses communication with Earth while a hardware module fails; it must preserve critical control before humans can intervene.
q: 最重要的 NFR 是什么？
q_en: What is the most important NFR?
options: fault tolerance
社交分享能力
广告点击率
界面主题可配置
options_en: Fault tolerance.
Social sharing.
Ad click-through rate.
Configurable UI themes.
why: 通信断开时不能依赖外部恢复，系统要靠冗余、隔离和本地恢复继续运行。这里可用性和安全都建立在容错能力上。
why_en: Fault tolerance dominates because the spacecraft must keep critical control locally when communication and hardware fail.
whenOtherWins: 如果是普通内容网站，成本和快速迭代可能比极端容错更优先。
tradeoff: 自主生存能力 vs 成本/复杂度

scenario: 你在比较一个请求是 CPU-bound、memory-bound 还是 IO-bound；只需要数量级，不需要精确 benchmark。
scenario_en: You are comparing whether a request is CPU-bound, memory-bound, or IO-bound; you only need order of magnitude, not an exact benchmark.
q: 哪个经验锚点最适合白板估算？
q_en: Which rule of thumb fits a whiteboard estimate?
options: CPU 任务为 X，内存约 10X，IO 约 100X
CPU、内存、磁盘总是同样快
磁盘 seek 通常比 CPU cache 访问更快
网络跨洲 RTT 可以忽略不计
options_en: If a CPU task is X, memory is roughly 10X and IO roughly 100X.
CPU, memory, and disk are always equally fast.
Disk seeks are usually faster than CPU cache access.
Cross-continent RTT can be ignored.
why: 这是数量级锚点：CPU 缓存/计算最快，内存慢一档，磁盘和网络 I/O 再慢很多。它会影响你是优化算法、缓存数据，还是减少远程/磁盘访问。
why_en: The CPU-memory-IO gap tells you whether to optimize computation, cache data, or remove disk and network hops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返时延，表示请求到达对端并收到响应的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-Trip Time is the time for a request to reach the peer and for the response to return.

scenario: 估算单台 64 核服务器处理简单 CPU 请求：假设每请求 350 万条指令、CPI=1、主频 3.5 GHz。
scenario_en: Estimate a 64-core server handling simple CPU requests: assume 3.5 million instructions per request, CPI=1, and a 3.5 GHz clock.
q: 64K RPS 粗估在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How should the 64K RPS estimate be used in design?
options: 作为服务器数量估算的分母，再用真实压测修正
当作所有请求类型永远成立的 SLA
替代峰值流量、缓存命中率和数据库瓶颈分析
证明单机一定能承接所有生产流量
options_en: Use it as the denominator for server-count estimates, then correct it with load tests.
Treat it as an SLA that holds for every request type forever.
Use it instead of analyzing peaks, cache hit rate, and database bottlenecks.
Use it to prove one machine can handle all production traffic.
why: CPU time = 3.5M × 1 / 3.5GHz = 0.001 秒，所以每核约 1,000 RPS，64 核约 64,000 RPS。这个数是后续估服务器数量的分母。
why_en: At 1 ms per request, one core handles about 1,000 RPS, so 64 cores give roughly 64,000 RPS for capacity estimates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，用来衡量服务吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requests Per Second measures how many requests a service handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条指令平均消耗的 CPU 时钟周期数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cycles Per Instruction is the average CPU cycles spent per instruction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 十亿赫兹，常用于表示 CPU 每秒时钟周期数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gigahertz means billions of clock cycles per second.

scenario: Twitter-like 服务有 500M DAU，每人每天 20 次请求；假设请求均匀分布，单机 64,000 RPS。
scenario_en: A Twitter-like service has 500M DAU and 20 requests per user per day; assume even distribution and 64,000 RPS per server.
q: 平均负载下服务器数估算给出什么警告？
q_en: What warning does the average-load server estimate give?
options: 把 2 台当下限，再建峰值模型
把 2 台当最终答案，不再看峰值和余量
DAU 不能用于任何估算，也不能转成 RPS
只要平均值够低，就不需要监控和压测
options_en: Treat two servers as a lower bound, then model peaks.
Treat two servers as final and ignore peaks and buffer.
DAU can never be converted into RPS for estimates.
If the average is low, monitoring and load tests are unnecessary.
why: 公式是 500M × 20 / 86,400 ≈ 115K RPS；115K / 64K ≈ 2 台。这个结果太乐观，说明平均值必须接峰值模型、监控和余量。
why_en: The average estimate gives about two servers, which is a sanity-check failure because real traffic is not evenly spread.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，表示一天内使用产品的独立用户数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Daily Active Users is the number of unique users active in one day.

scenario: 同一个 Twitter-like 服务每天 10B 请求；若用 80/20 假设：80% 流量集中在一天 20% 的时间，即 4.8 小时；单机 64,000 RPS。
scenario_en: The same Twitter-like service has 10B requests/day; with an 80/20 assumption, 80% of traffic lands in 20% of the day, or 4.8 hours; each server handles 64,000 RPS.
q: 80/20 峰值模型改变了什么判断？
q_en: What judgment does the 80/20 peak model change?
options: 把平均容量改成更接近峰值窗口的容量
证明平均流量模型已经足够，不用看峰值
证明所有日请求都会挤在同一秒发生
说明服务器数量和流量分布没有关系
options_en: It turns the average-capacity estimate into a peak-window estimate.
It proves the average traffic model is enough and peaks can be ignored.
It proves every daily request arrives in the same second.
It says server count is unrelated to traffic distribution.
why: 公式是 0.8 × 10B / (4.8 × 3600) ≈ 463K RPS；463K / 64K ≈ 7.2，向上取约 8 台。它用于把平均负载改成更像真实的峰值容量。
why_en: The 80/20 peak model gives about 8 servers and is a better capacity input than a flat daily average.

scenario: Twitter-like 服务：500M DAU，每人每天 3 条 tweet；每条 250B 元数据，10% 带 200KB 图片，5% 带 3MB 视频。
scenario_en: A Twitter-like service has 500M DAU, 3 tweets per user per day, 250B metadata per tweet, 10% with a 200KB image, and 5% with a 3MB video.
q: 每日存储量为什么由媒体主导？
q_en: Why is daily storage dominated by media?
options: 按文本、图片、视频分别相乘，视频项主导容量
文本一定比视频大，因为每条 tweet 都有文字
图片和视频比例不影响存储，只看用户数
只需要算 tweet 条数，不需要对象大小
options_en: Multiply text, image, and video terms separately, and the video term dominates.
Text is always larger than video because every tweet has text.
Image and video ratios do not affect storage; only user count matters.
Only tweet count matters, and object size is irrelevant.
why: 公式是 1.5B tweets/day 分别乘以对象大小和媒体比例；视频对象虽然只占 5%，但 3MB 远大于文本。这个数会决定 blob storage、保留期和带宽预算。
why_en: Media dominates because object size overwhelms count, driving blob storage, retention, and bandwidth planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 太字节，约等于 10^12 字节，常用于存储估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A terabyte is about 10^12 bytes and is commonly used in storage estimates.

scenario: 服务每天写入约 255TB 媒体和文本数据；要估算平均入站带宽，按一天 86,400 秒，字节转 bit 乘 8。
scenario_en: A service ingests about 255TB of media and text per day; estimate average inbound bandwidth using 86,400 seconds per day and multiply bytes by 8 for bits.
q: 24 Gbps 入站估算约束哪条路径？
q_en: Which path does the 24 Gbps ingress estimate constrain?
options: 上传入口、网络链路和对象存储写入能力
只约束前端按钮颜色和页面布局
只约束离线推荐模型训练指标
说明出站视频播放带宽一定为零
options_en: Upload ingress, network links, and object-store write capacity.
Only frontend button colors and page layout.
Only offline recommendation-training metrics.
It means outbound video playback bandwidth is zero.
why: 公式是 255 × 10^12 bytes / 86,400 × 8 ≈ 24 × 10^9 bit/s。这个数是网络、入口代理和对象存储写入能力的起点。
why_en: Dividing daily bytes by seconds and multiplying by 8 gives about 24 Gbps, the starting point for ingress and storage capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒十亿比特，常用于网络带宽估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gigabits per second measures network bandwidth in billions of bits per second.

scenario: 你在做容量草算，需要把机器角色和主要资源压力对应起来，而不是把所有服务器都当同一种盒子。
scenario_en: You are doing a capacity estimate and need to map server roles to their dominant resource pressure instead of treating every server as the same box.
q: 哪些角色映射合理？
q_en: Which role mappings are reasonable?
options: Web server：接负载均衡后的 API 入口，CPU 和网络更关键
Application server：跑业务逻辑和动态内容，CPU/内存压力更大
Storage server：优先提供大容量持久存储
Storage server：一定比所有缓存服务器低延迟
options_en: Web server: API entry point after load balancing, with CPU and network pressure.
Application server: runs business logic and dynamic content, often heavier on CPU and memory.
Storage server: prioritizes large persistent capacity.
Storage server: always lower latency than every cache server.
why: 不同角色的瓶颈不同：入口看连接和 CPU，业务层看逻辑计算，存储层看容量、I/O 和耐久性。混成一种机器会让估算失真。
why_en: Server roles have different bottlenecks, so capacity estimates should separate entry, business logic, and storage pressure.

scenario: 你要把一个大文件上传平台拆成常见 building blocks：用户上传大视频，后台转码，客户端下载热门视频，服务要限流和监控。
scenario_en: You are decomposing a large-file upload platform into building blocks: users upload videos, background jobs transcode them, clients download popular videos, and the service needs rate limiting and monitoring.
q: 哪组 building blocks 最贴合主路径？
q_en: Which set of building blocks best fits the main path?
options: 大对象存储、异步任务、边缘缓存、限流监控
只用单机数组和 cron，所有视频都放进内存
只用 DNS，不需要任何持久存储或后台任务
只用关系型事务，不需要转码和下载缓存
options_en: Large-object storage, async tasks, edge caching, rate limiting, and monitoring.
Only one in-memory array and cron, with all videos in memory.
Only DNS, with no persistent storage or background jobs.
Only relational transactions, with no transcoding or download cache.
why: 视频是大对象，先落 blob store；转码是异步重任务，交给任务调度；热门下载走 CDN，入口用限流保护，监控看错误和延迟。
why_en: Large videos need blob storage, async transcoding needs task scheduling, popular downloads need a CDN, and rate limiting plus monitoring protect operations.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是小文本 CRUD，关系型数据库和简单后台任务可能足够。
tradeoff: 专用 building blocks vs 单体简化
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["Uploader"] --> RL["Rate limiter"]
    RL --> Blob["Blob store"]
    Blob --> Scheduler["Task scheduler"]
    Scheduler --> Worker["Transcode workers"]
    Blob --> CDN["CDN"]
    CDN --> Viewer["Viewer"]
    RL --> Mon["Monitoring"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器按用户、服务或令牌桶限制请求速率，保护下游不过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limiter caps request rates by user, service, or token bucket to protect downstream systems.
